questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Freundlich adsorption isotherm $\frac{x}{m} = k P^{1/n}$, a linear plot of $\log_{10}(x/m)$ versus $\log_{10} P$ has slope $0.40$ and $y$-intercept $0.301$. The values of $n$ and $k$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: Taking $\log_{10}$ gives $\log_{10}(x/m) = \log_{10} k + \frac{1}{n}\log_{10} P$. Thus $1/n = 0.40 \implies n = 2.5$, and $\log_{10} k = 0.301 \implies k = 10^{0.301} = 2.0$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Upon diluting an aqueous solution of a weak electrolyte such as $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ with pure water at constant temperature,
optionsEn: specific conductivity ($\kappa$) decreases while molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) increases sharply.
specific conductivity ($\kappa$) increases while molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) decreases.
both specific conductivity ($\kappa$) and molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) remain constant.
both specific conductivity ($\kappa$) and molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) increase.
questions.explanationEn: Dilution reduces the number of charge-carrying ions per unit volume, so specific conductivity $\kappa$ decreases. Simultaneously, the degree of dissociation $\alpha$ rises sharply (Ostwald dilution law) and volume per mole increases, so $\Lambda_m = \kappa/c$ increases sharply.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following characteristics is typical of **chemisorption** rather than physisorption?
optionsEn: Reversible adsorption governed purely by weak dispersion forces with negligible activation energy
Enthalpy of adsorption in the range $-80$ to $-400\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and high chemical specificity
Formation of multimolecular layers at high pressures
Decrease in extent of adsorption monotonically with increasing temperature starting from $0\text{ K}$
questions.explanationEn: Chemisorption involves chemical bond formation between adsorbate and surface, so it is highly specific, limited to a monolayer, often activated, and exhibits large exothermic enthalpies of adsorption ($80\text{--}400\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the gas-phase reaction $2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(\text{g}) \to 4\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})$, if the rate of appearance of $\text{NO}_2$ is $2.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$, the rate of disappearance of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$, $-\frac{d[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]}{dt}$, is
questions.explanationEn: From stoichiometry, $-\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]}{dt} = \frac{1}{4}\frac{d[\text{NO}_2]}{dt}$. Therefore, $-\frac{d[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\left(2.4 \times 10^{-3}\right) = 1.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the Gibbs adsorption equation $\Gamma_2 = -\frac{c}{RT}\left(\frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial c}\right)_T$, a solute that **lowers** the surface tension $\gamma$ of water with increasing concentration $c$ exhibits
optionsEn: negative surface excess ($\Gamma_2 < 0$), meaning depletion at the interface.
positive surface excess ($\Gamma_2 > 0$), meaning accumulation at the air–water interface.
zero surface excess ($\Gamma_2 = 0$), meaning uniform concentration throughout.
questions.explanationEn: If $\left(\frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial c}\right)_T < 0$, then $\Gamma_2 = -\frac{c}{RT}\left(\frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial c}\right)_T > 0$, indicating positive adsorption (enrichment) of the solute at the interface.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A reactant $A$ decomposes via two parallel first-order pathways: $A \xrightarrow{k_1} B$ ($E_{a1} = 40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and $A \xrightarrow{k_2} C$ ($E_{a2} = 80\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). At $300\text{ K}$, $k_1 = 3 k_2$. The overall apparent activation energy $E_{a,\text{eff}}$ for the disappearance of $A$ at $300\text{ K}$ is
questions.explanationEn: For parallel first-order reactions, $k_{\text{eff}} = k_1 + k_2$, and $E_{a,\text{eff}} = RT^2 \frac{d\ln(k_1 + k_2)}{dT} = \frac{k_1 E_{a1} + k_2 E_{a2}}{k_1 + k_2}$. Substituting $k_1 = 3k_2$: $E_{a,\text{eff}} = \frac{3(40) + 1(80)}{3 + 1} = \frac{200}{4} = 50\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Adsorption of $\text{N}_2$ on a solid follows the Langmuir isotherm $\frac{P}{V} = \frac{1}{K V_m} + \frac{P}{V_m}$. A linear plot of $P/V$ (in $\text{bar cm}^{-3}$) against $P$ (in $\text{bar}$) gives a slope of $0.025\text{ cm}^{-3}$ and a $y$-intercept of $0.050\text{ bar cm}^{-3}$. The monolayer volume $V_m$ and adsorption constant $K$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: From $\frac{P}{V} = \frac{1}{K V_m} + \frac{1}{V_m}P$: slope $= 1/V_m = 0.025\text{ cm}^{-3} \implies V_m = 40\text{ cm}^3$. The ratio $\text{slope}/\text{intercept} = K = 0.025 / 0.050 = 0.50\text{ bar}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the reversible first-order isomerization $A \xrightleftharpoons[k_b]{k_f} B$ starting with $[A]_0 = 1.0\text{ M}$ and $[B]_0 = 0$. If $k_f = 3.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$ and $k_b = 1.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, the relaxation time $\tau$ and equilibrium concentration $[A]_{\text{eq}}$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: For $A \xrightleftharpoons[k_b]{k_f} B$, the relaxation rate constant is $k_r = k_f + k_b = 0.04\text{ s}^{-1}$, so $\tau = \frac{1}{k_f + k_b} = \frac{1}{0.04} = 25\text{ s}$. At equilibrium, $K = \frac{[B]_{\text{eq}}}{[A]_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{k_f}{k_b} = 3$, and $[A]_{\text{eq}} + [B]_{\text{eq}} = 1.0\text{ M} \implies [A]_{\text{eq}} = \frac{1.0}{1+3} = 0.25\text{ M}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the second-order reaction $A + B \to P$ with rate law $r = k[A][B]$ and unequal initial concentrations $[A]_0 = a$, $[B]_0 = b$ ($a > b$), which plot yields a straight line passing through the origin?
questions.explanationEn: Integrating $\frac{dx}{(a-x)(b-x)} = k\,dt$ yields $\frac{1}{a-b}\ln\left(\frac{b(a-x)}{a(b-x)}\right) = kt$. At $t = 0$ ($x = 0$), $\ln\left(\frac{ba}{ab}\right) = \ln 1 = 0$, so plotting $\ln\left(\frac{b(a-x)}{a(b-x)}\right)$ versus $t$ gives a straight line through the origin with slope $(a-b)k$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the consecutive first-order sequence $A \xrightarrow{k} B \xrightarrow{k} C$ with equal rate constants ($k_1 = k_2 = k$) and initial concentrations $[A]_0 = a$, $[B]_0 = [C]_0 = 0$, the maximum concentration of intermediate $B$ is
questions.explanationEn: When $k_1 = k_2 = k$, integrating $\frac{d[B]}{dt} + k[B] = ka e^{-kt}$ yields $[B]_t = akt e^{-kt}$. Setting $\frac{d[B]}{dt} = ak(1 - kt)e^{-kt} = 0$ gives $t_{\max} = 1/k$, where $[B]_{\max} = a(1)e^{-1} = a/e$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a reversible galvanic cell $\text{Zn}(s)\,|\,\text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq})\,||\,\text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq})\,|\,\text{Cu}(s)$ at $298\text{ K}$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: Doubling the stoichiometric coefficients of the cell reaction doubles $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$.
questions.explanationEn: $E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{RT}{2F}\ln\frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]}$, so (A), (B), and (D) are true. Electrode/cell potential is an **intensive** property ($E^\circ = -\Delta G^\circ / nF$), so scaling the equation leaves $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ unchanged, making (C) false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) correctly describe(s) physisorption of a gas on a solid surface?
optionsEn: It is accompanied by a decrease in entropy of the adsorbate ($\Delta S_{\text{ads}} < 0$).
Because adsorption is spontaneous ($\Delta G_{\text{ads}} < 0$) and $\Delta S_{\text{ads}} < 0$, it must be exothermic ($\Delta H_{\text{ads}} < 0$).
Higher critical temperature ($T_c$) gases generally undergo greater physisorption at a given $T$ and $P$.
It requires a high activation energy comparable to covalent bond dissociation energies.
questions.explanationEn: Adsorption restricts translational freedom ($\Delta S_{\text{ads}} < 0$), so spontaneity ($\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$) requires $\Delta H_{\text{ads}} < 0$ (A, B true). Easily liquefiable gases (higher $T_c$, stronger van der Waals forces) physisorb more readily (C true). Physisorption has negligible activation energy (D false).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Regarding ionic mobility $u_i$ in aqueous solution at $298\text{ K}$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The limiting molar ionic conductivity is related to mobility by $\lambda_i^\circ = |z_i| F u_i^\circ$.
Among alkali metal cations, the hydrodynamic (Stokes) radius follows $\text{Li}^+ > \text{Na}^+ > \text{K}^+ > \text{Cs}^+$.
The drift velocity of an ion in a uniform electric field $E$ is $v_d = u_i E$.
Because $\text{Li}^+$ has the smallest bare crystallographic radius, it has the highest ionic mobility in water.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. Because bare $\text{Li}^+$ has the highest charge density, it holds the largest hydration shell and therefore has the **lowest** ionic mobility in water among alkali cations, making (D) false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For parallel first-order reactions $B \xleftarrow{k_1} A \xrightarrow{k_2} C$ starting with pure $A$ ($[A]_0 = a$, $[B]_0 = [C]_0 = 0$), the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The overall half-life of $A$ is $\dfrac{\ln 2}{k_1 + k_2}$.
The ratio $[B]_t / [C]_t$ equals $k_1 / k_2$ at all times $t > 0$.
The fractional yield of $B$ at $t \to \infty$ is $\dfrac{k_1}{k_1 + k_2}$.
If $E_{a1} > E_{a2}$, raising the temperature increases the branching ratio $[B]/[C]$.
questions.explanationEn: All four statements are correct: $[A]_t = a e^{-(k_1+k_2)t}$ gives $t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k_1+k_2}$; $[B]_t/[C]_t = k_1/k_2$ is time-independent; final yield of $B$ is $k_1/(k_1+k_2)$; and since $\frac{d\ln(k_1/k_2)}{dT} = \frac{E_{a1}-E_{a2}}{RT^2} > 0$, increasing $T$ favors the higher-barrier pathway $B$.

questions.questionTextEn: In an aqueous solution of $\text{NaNO}_3$, the transport number of $\text{Na}^+$ is $0.412$. The transport number of $\text{NO}_3^-$ is _______. *(round off to three decimal places)*

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The reversible first-order reaction $A \xrightleftharpoons[k_b]{k_f} B$ has a relaxation time $\tau = 10\text{ s}$ and a forward rate constant $k_f = 0.080\text{ s}^{-1}$. The equilibrium constant $K = [B]_{\text{eq}}/[A]_{\text{eq}}$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The specific conductivity of a $0.050\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ aqueous electrolyte solution at $298\text{ K}$ is $2.50 \times 10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$. Its molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is _______ $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: $\Lambda_m = \frac{1000\,\kappa}{c} = \frac{1000 \times 2.50 \times 10^{-3}}{0.050} = 50\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The rate constant of a chemical reaction doubles when the temperature is raised from $300\text{ K}$ to $310\text{ K}$. Using $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the Arrhenius activation energy $E_a$ is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: $E_a = \frac{R T_1 T_2}{T_2 - T_1}\ln\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{8.314 \times 300 \times 310}{10}\ln 2 = 53594.3\text{ J mol}^{-1} = 53.59\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \approx 53.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry III: Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry & Adsorption (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the consecutive first-order reaction $A \xrightarrow{k_1} B \xrightarrow{k_2} C$ with $k_1 = 0.20\text{ min}^{-1}$, $k_2 = 0.05\text{ min}^{-1}$, $[A]_0 = 1.00\text{ M}$, and $[B]_0 = [C]_0 = 0$, the concentration of intermediate $B$ at $t = 10.0\text{ min}$ is _______ $\text{M}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
